newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Threat of opposition unrest looms over Bangladesh.
newsitem.headline: Threat of opposition unrest looms over Bangladesh.

text.p: Bangladesh's main opposition party on Thursday renewed threats of nationwide unrest to topple the government unless it "comes to its senses".

"We are setting a March 31 deadline for the government to meet all our demands, including ending the repression of opposition and selling out our national interest to foreign masters," Bangladesh national Party (BNP) secretary-general Abdul Mannan Bhuiyan told reporters.
"Our party will organise countrywide protests and rallies beginning on March 3, and we believe the government will come to its senses and start behaving politically," he said.
"If the government misses the deadline, we will be forced to launch a tougher programme," Mannan said without elaborating.
Political analysts said he was hinting at the possibility of calling general strikes and other unrest to build pressure on Hasina's nascent administration.
Hasina's Awami League came to power after elections in June last year.

Mannan said the government had "failed to keep prices of essential goods under control, had cracked down on political foes, arrested thousands of opposition activists and allowed law and order to deteriorate".

BNP chief Begum Khaleda Zia told a party rally in southeastern town of Feni on Wednesday that March 3 would mark the beginning of a countrywide movement to oust the government of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.

"We no longer find reasons to support the corrupt, inefficient and repressive government," Khaleda said. "It has gone all the way to sell the national interest to big brothers in a neighbouring country," she added, apparently referring to India.
Independent analysts said the BNP was looking for a pretext to destabilise Hasina's government, which has been praised by international donors for creating a transparent administration.

Both Khaleda and Mannan criticised Hasina for allegedly trying to grant India a land corridor to enable it to transport supplies and troops to India's northeastern states where New Delhi is battling insurgents.
"These are all part of a blueprint to satisfy Indian hegemonist designs," Khaleda said.

Mannan described a recent treaty between Dhaka and New Delhi to share water from the Ganges river as "unequal in favour of India", and said a proposal to create a sub-regional forum involving India, Nepal and Bhutan was "dangerous for Bangladesh's economic independence".
"We will resist them at all costs," Mannan added.
